name: Sika Waterbar FB-125
paste:
SIKA WATERBAR® FB-125: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika Waterbar® FB-125, February 2026, Version 03.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/q/sika-waterbar-fb-125.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika Waterbar® FB-125 where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (February 2026, Version 03.01).
1.2 Product description. Sika Waterbar® FB-125 is a hybrid waterstop with a rough textured surface based on flexible polyolefin (FPO). The waterstop is placed into the fresh concrete and becomes fully embedded in the cured concrete. It provides a fully bonded, durable watertight seal, that prevents any lateral water underflow.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. It is designed to seal construction joints as an internal waterstop in watertight concrete constructions. Typical applications:
    - Underground structures and basements
    - Water retaining structures
    - Water treatment plants
    - Swimming pools
    - Reservoirs
    - Retaining walls
    - Connection from old to new structures
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.6.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika Waterbar® FB-125
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Bonded flexible waterstop for sealing construction joints
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Certificates and test reports.
    - Tests according to EAD 320002-02-0605, ofi, Report No. 2101089_E
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EAD 320002-02-0605: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - EN 1849-2: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Mass per area (p.1); Product Information > Thickness (p.1); Product Information > Total width (p.1).
    - DIN 53505: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shore A hardness (p.2).
    - EN 12311-2: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile strength (p.2).
    - EN 13501-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Reaction to fire (p.2).
    - EN 1928: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Watertightness (p.2).
    - ASTM D5385: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Resistance to lateral water migration (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Bonded to concrete structure - no lateral water underflow
    - Permanent flexibility
    - Quick and easy to install
    - Long rolls reduce the number of joins
    - No special tools and equipment required
    - No extra recess and detailing of reinforcement
    - No obstructions for concreting
    - Fully bonded for easy repair in case of leakage
    - Resistant to all natural substances in soil and groundwater
    - Durable and robust system
    - Can be combined with other proven Sika waterproofing / joint sealing systems
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Hybrid based on flexible polyolefin (FPO)
    - Appearance and colour: Light grey, rough textured surface
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Mass per area: 4.1 kg/m² (-5 / +10 %) (EN 1849-2)
    - Total width: > 120 mm (EN 1849-2)
    - Shore A hardness: 85 ± 10 % (DIN 53505)
    - Tensile strength: ≥ 6 N/mm² (EN 12311-2)
    - Elongation: ≥ 400 %
    - Reaction to fire: Class E (EN 13501-1)
    - Watertightness: Tight (EN 1928)
    - Service temperature: -10 °C min. / +40 °C max.
    - Adhesion in peel: ≥ 50 N / 50 mm
    - Resistance to lateral water migration: Pass (7 bar, 7 days) (ASTM D5385 / D5385M)
2.7 System structure. Accessories used for fixing and installation:
    - SikaProof® Sandwich Tape-50
    - Mounting brackets
    - Clamping bar set
2.8 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: Single roll of 50 m wrapped in foil
    - Shelf life: 36 months from date of production
2.9 Storage conditions. Product must be stored in original unopened and undamaged packaging in dry conditions and temperatures between +5 °C and +30 °C. Store in a horizontal position. Do not stack pallets of the rolls on top of each other, or under pallets of any other materials during transport or storage. Always refer to packaging.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 Substrate preparation. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (February 2026, Version 03.01) states no substrate preparation requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (February 2026, Version 03.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Thickness: > 3.00 mm (EN 1849-2)
4.3 Application. Strictly follow installation procedures as defined in method statements and working instructions which must always be adjusted to the actual site conditions.
4.4 Application - Jointing. Sika Waterbar® FB-125 is jointed by:
    - Thermal welding equipment
    - Adhered with SikaProof® Sandwich Tape-50
    - Mechanically fixed with a clamping bar set
4.5 Application - Installation.
    - Embed the waterstop at least 30 mm into the fresh concrete to prevent lateral water underflow.
    - There are two methods for installing and casting the waterbar (choose the most suitable method for your application):
    - Option A: Standard Method (Most common for slab-wall, slab-slab, or wall-wall applications)
    - 1. Pre-install the waterbar to the reinforcement to keep it in place.
    - 2. Pour the concrete (use a plywood or cardboard protection between the rebars and the waterbar to keep the waterbar clean).
    - 3. Clean the waterbar to remove any concrete residues, if needed.
    - Option B: Simplified Method (Mainly for slab-wall applications)
    - 1.Temporarily fix the waterstop to the starter bars. 2. Shake the waterstop into the fresh concrete.
    - 3. Secure the waterstop in the fresh concrete with a mounting bracket to keep it upright.
4.6 Limitations and important considerations. Installation work must only be carried out by contractors, experienced in this type of application.
    - The Product is not permanently UV and weather resistant. Concrete must be placed within a maximum of 90 days after installation. Otherwise the Product must be protected with appropriate protection sheets.
    - A minimal embedment of 30 mm into the fresh concrete must be ensured to prevent lateral water underflow.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, confirm the site conditions with the manufacturer. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions to be verified. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (February 2026, Version 03.01) lists no application condition limits.
5.3 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Thickness: > 3.00 mm (EN 1849-2)
    - Mass per area: 4.1 kg/m² (-5 / +10 %) (EN 1849-2)
    - Total width: > 120 mm (EN 1849-2)
    - Shore A hardness: 85 ± 10 % (DIN 53505)
    - Tensile strength: ≥ 6 N/mm² (EN 12311-2)
    - Reaction to fire: Class E (EN 13501-1)
    - Watertightness: Tight (EN 1928)
    - Resistance to lateral water migration: Pass (7 bar, 7 days) (ASTM D5385 / D5385M)
5.4 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.5 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika Waterbar® FB-125, February 2026, Version 03.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/q/sika-waterbar-fb-125.pdf
    - Brochure: Sika Waterbar FB-125 Product Flyer.pdf, version 19/03/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/a/Leaflet-Sika-Waterbar-FB-125%20AU%202026%20FIN%20DIGI.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. This product is an article as defined in article 3 of regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 (REACH). It contains no substances which are intended to be released from the article under normal or reasonably foreseeable conditions of use. A safety data sheet following article 31 of the same regulation is not needed to bring the product to the market, to transport or to use it. For safe use follow the instructions given in the product data sheet. Based on our current knowledge, this product does not contain SVHC (substances of very high concern) as listed in Annex XIV of the REACH regulation or on the candidate list published by the European Chemicals Agency in concentrations above 0,1 % (w/w).
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.1, and include the records in the project documentation.
